_comment: The one place MakeMKV's version, checksums and download locations are written down.
Read by server/riparr/makemkv.py and by tools/makemkv-install.sh, so the service and
the root installer can never disagree about what they are fetching.
Mirrors exist because makemkv.com is unreliable -- it was down for the whole of
August 2026 -- and an appliance whose setup cannot complete because somebody else's
web server is having a month is not an appliance. They are tried in order and the
first one whose bytes match sha256 wins.
A mirror is safe precisely because of that hash. It is pinned here, in the repository,
and checked after every download; a mirror serving the wrong file -- stale, truncated
or hostile -- fails the check and the next one is tried. So adding mirrors costs
nothing in trust. Removing the hash would cost everything.
PROVENANCE (2026-10-01, 2.0.0). Fetched from makemkv.com itself, which by then served
only 2.0.0 and answered 404 for 1.18.4. Confirmed independently twice over:
- the Internet Archive's 2026-09-22 capture of the same /download/ URLs
Three sources, one pair of hashes. The licence and EULA differ from 1.18.4 only in
the copyright year, and the item attribute IDs Riparr reads are unchanged.
